angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 536,385 km at 48.19 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 15578: distance 48.189 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 48.189 +/- 0.578 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 20.9561 +/- 0.0128 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94), 1643.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 0.771 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 15578: radius 0.771 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.267 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 536,385 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4729 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 15578: effective temperature 4729 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 15578: effective temperature 4729 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 20868 (pscomppars): spectral type K3/4 IV, from Moutou et al. 2009 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009A&A...496..513M/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 20868: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 20868 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.05 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 20868 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.529, from Moutou et al. 2009 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009A&A...496..513M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 20868 (pscomppars): age 4.5 Gyr, from Moutou et al. 2009 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009A&A...496..513M/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 20868 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.1 km/s, from Moutou et al. 2009 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009A&A...496..513M/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 4.9 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 8 published values span log g 4.12 to 4.9, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.6% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
